color.name: Color and Composition
color.v1_3_note: Renamed from 'Color: Perception, Not Physics'. As of spine v1.3, this sequence absorbs the composition study and is sourced from three auto-research galleries: primitive-stack, pattern, and facade.

composition_sources.role: vertical compositions — stacks of primitives as raw composition vocabulary
plane compositions — wallpaper-group repetitions across the grid
architectural compositions — facades as composed parts within a frame

color.truth: Color is perception, not physics. RGB is a lie we agree on. What you see depends on context, not wavelength alone.
color.qfep_connection: Color is a system stateâ€”part of the S term in QFEP. But unlike vectors, color is fundamentally perceptual: the same wavelength can appear different colors depending on surrounding context. Color reveals the gap between ontology (photons) and experience (qualia).

color.description: The physics and perception of color. Light has wavelength, but color is what brains make of it. Explore RGB, HSV, and the gap between objective light and subjective experience.
learning_objectives: RGB color space: additive mixing of red, green, blue
HSV color space: hue, saturation, valueâ€”more intuitive
Perception theory: color constancy, simultaneous contrast
Digital materiality: how screens create color

Color as function: every gradient is a function from t ∈ [0,1] to a color. Color is your first encounter with a continuous mapping — the move that sets up wavefunctions (functions of time) and forces (vector-valued functions of position) as already-familiar.
color.deferred_reason: Removed from active sequence to tighten progression. Color_Context is a 30-artifact showcase map â€” potential future standalone or advanced color sequence.

artifact_groups.rationale: Nail salon studio: precise color selection on a digital body. Introduces color as interaction.
Grid becomes canvas: systematic color assignment cell by cell with spectrum visualization.
Walking through light: spectrum progression with animated rainbow emitters along a corridor.
Pillar gauntlet: color collection, mixing, and spectrum analysis in a columned runway.
Action painting studio: gestural color application meets structured Albers color studies.
Gradient environment: continuous color transitions dissolving categorical boundaries.
MultiMesh color cycling test: pattern progression through flashlight interaction. Synthesis of color systems.
